title: Phased-Launch Orchestration: Guardrails, Signal Maps, and Decision Automations
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Purpose: Create a reusable, operations-ready blueprint for orchestrating phased launches (internal shadow -> small canary -> graduated ramp -> full commit) with explicit signal ownership, automated decision automation hooks, and prescriptive rollback thresholds. Scope: playbook, decision matrix, minimum instrumentation set, sample-size/temporal windows for metric evaluation, Grafana dashboards and alert rules, guardrail automation (circuit-breaker + feature-flag integration), and handoff checklist for Product, Eng, and Design. Outcomes: reduced incident blast radius, repeatable launch cadence across features (API, console, runtime), and standard artifacts for audit/compliance.

Key elements to define: hypothesis template; primary/secondary/guardrail metrics; ownership (who owns metric health during each stage); minimum telemetry (latency p50/p95, error/yield, quality eval on golden prompts, token-cost per request, infra capacity headroom); gating logic (absolute thresholds, relative delta against baseline, and statistical significance rules); automated actions (scale-down, auto-fallback to stable model variant, traffic cut, rollback to previous release); human-in-the-loop escalation paths and post-mortem timeline.

Instrumentation & tooling: tie experiment lifecycle to Redwood Console routes and per-route dashboards (link to dashboard skeleton in Confluence), add Eval harness job templates (reference: drive/experiments/eval-templates), add canary-specific tracing span ids and end-to-end synthetic checks. Integrations: feature-flag provider (launchdarkly/ff-internal), CI job for synthetic smoke on every deploy, alerting via PagerDuty escalation for P0/P1 breaches.

Trade-offs considered: strict statistical gates increase time-to-rollout for low-traffic features; looser heuristic thresholds shorten time-to-value but increase operational risk. Recommendation: mix hard guardrails for high-risk metrics (errors, security) with adaptive relative thresholds for quality metrics, plus automatic traffic throttling to protect SLOs.

Artifacts to produce: playbook doc (Confluence), decision matrix CSV, Grafana dashboards (templated), alert rules in Terraform, two example run-throughs (text-generation change + model-variant fallback), demo runbook for SRE on-call use. Links: CONFLUENCE: https://redwood.company/confluence/experimentation/pm-25011-playbook, DRIVE: https://drive.redwood.company/experiments/eval-templates, GH PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4421
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published with step-by-step staged checklist and decision matrix
Grafana dashboards and alert rules checked into infra repo and runnable in staging
Automated gating hooks implemented for at least two actions: traffic cut and auto-fallback to stable model variant
Minimum instrumentation (latency, error rates, quality eval) available for new experiments and shown in Console mockups
Two example experiments executed end-to-end in staging following the playbook (logs, metrics, and post-mortems recorded)

notes: Minimum sample guidance: for <1000 daily requests use 72-hour window and a relative-delta threshold; for >=1000 daily requests use 24-hour windows plus standard p-value check

Guardrail thresholds (initial): error-rate absolute >0.5% triggers immediate traffic cut; latency p95 increase >40% triggers adaptive throttling; quality regression >5% on golden-set triggers manual review
Decision automation: use a two-step action (auto-throttle then evaluate for 15 minutes; if condition persists, auto-cut traffic and page on-call)

Cross-team owners: Product (experiment hypothesis & success criteria), Eng (gating automation and instrumentation), Design (eval prompt selection and UX visibility), SRE (runbook and on-call escalation)
Follow-ups: add a lightweight template to create signal maps when authoring new experiments; add a checklist item to PR template linking the experiment ID to Console route
